title: UK government accepts AI healthcare recommendations
key_facts: The UK government accepted all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare.
In September the commission, led by NHS doctors, recommended continuous monitoring of AI medical devices through their working life instead of one-time assessment.
The third phase of the AI Airlock regulatory sandbox will test how to manage post-market surveillance.
The MHRA, the medicines and devices regulator, will publish draft guidance on managing device changes in December 2026 and consult on classifying AI devices.
Ministers are exploring staged authorisation routes for earlier NHS access under close supervision while real-world evidence is gathered.
Health innovation minister James Frith said innovation must never come at the expense of patient safety.
quote_evidence: This means that British ministers will work to implement all 44 recommendations made by the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare
"We are acting now by accepting in full all 44 recommendations of the Independent Commission," Frith said.
why_it_matters_hint: Moves medical AI in Britain from one-off approval to ongoing monitoring, with staged earlier use in the NHS.
